newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo jewelry maker urges crackdown on smugglers.
newsitem.headline: Yugo jewelry maker urges crackdown on smugglers.

text.p: Yugoslavia's biggest gold jewelry maker Zlatara Majdanpek has called for a halt to gold jewelry smuggling which short-changes state coffers and stifles local production, Belgrade daily Politika said on Thursday.
"We urge you to halt the smuggling of gold jewelry which has taken frightening proportions," Zlatara's general manager Filip Vukovic was quoted as saying in a letter to the government.
Vukovic said all domestic producers were suffering greatly from the smuggling, which was costing the country 80 million German marks ($43.7 million) a year in unpaid taxes.
Zlatara called on the government to enforce strict measures to protect domestic jewelry producers from smuggling.
The gold jewelry producers group in the Yugoslav Chamber of Commerce, which has some 20 percent of the country's 2,500 registered jewellers, joined Zlatara in calls for stricter state measures.
The smugglers sell a gram of gold jewelry for 20 German marks even though calculations show that legally, it cannot be sold below 36 marks, Vukovic said.
"This means they have avoided paying taxes and are now competing with those who have," Vukovic said.
Domestic gold makers also called for further reduction of state duties to make domestic prices more competitive.
Taxes on domestic jewelry were cut from 80 to 36 percent at the beginning of 1997 but Majdanpek says duties are still high compared to other countries.
Majdanpek sources said the quantity of jewelry brought into the country is five times the Majdanpek production, but gave no production figures.

The jewelry, smuggled mainly from Hungary, Macedonia, Italy and Turkey, enters Yugoslavia via Montenegro, Kosovo and Bosnian Serb republic, the paper said. -- Beti Bilandzic, Belgrade newsroom 381 11 381 43 05 ($ = 1.831 German Marks)
